title: Degreewise-injective ordinary etale support sequence
statement:
Let $i:Z\hookrightarrow P$ be a closed immersion of schemes with complementary open immersion $j:U\hookrightarrow P$, and let $A$ be a finite commutative ring [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. Use ordinary derived categories of constant-$A$ module sheaves on small etale sites [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. For a module sheaf $M$ put $H_A(M)=i^*\ker(M\to j_*j^*M)$, where the map is the open adjunction unit. The canonical supported-sheaf isomorphism identifies this kernel with $i_*H_A(M)$, and its inclusion is the counit of $i_*\dashv H_A$. Let $I$ be a degreewise-injective K-injective cochain complex representing $L\in D(P_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ [def-pur-kinjective-complex]. Then
$$0\to i_*H_A(I)\to I\to j_*j^*I\to0$$
is a degreewise short exact sequence of complexes, natural in chain maps between such $I$. The complex $H_A(I)$ represents $Ri_A^!L$, the ordinary right adjoint of $i_*$, and $j_*j^*I$ represents $Rj_*j^*L$. The associated short-exact-sequence triangle, including its natural connecting morphism, realizes the counit/unit support triangle of [lem-exc-closed-support-triangle]. No injectivity after forgetting coefficient scalars is assumed.

proof.text: Put $G(M)=\ker(\eta_{j,M})$, so $H_A(M)=i^*G(M)$. Module kernels are sectionwise and module cokernels are the abelian ones [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]; module inverse images, direct images and their units have the underlying abelian functors and units [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact], [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]. So $G(M)$ is an $A$-submodule, and the isomorphism $q_M:G(M)\xrightarrow{\sim}i_*i^*G(M)=i_*H_A(M)$ of [lem-pur-etale-supported-kernel-adjunction], the closed unit at $G(M)$, is $A$-linear, as is its inverse. Module $i_*$ is exact: forgetting scalars is exact, faithful and reflects exactness, it commutes with $i_*$, and abelian $i_*$ is exact by [lem-pur-etale-supported-kernel-adjunction]. Next $j^*i_*N=0$: for $V$ etale over $U$, $(j^*i_*N)(V)=N(V\times_PZ)=N(\emptyset)=0$ by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-inverse-image-restriction] and [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]. For a module map $f:i_*N\to M$, naturality of the unit gives $\eta_{j,M}f=j_*j^*(f)\,\eta_{j,i_*N}=0$, so $f$ factors uniquely through $G(M)$. Abelian $i_*$ is fully faithful [lem-kun-04ca], so $q_M$ composed with this factorization is $i_*g$ for a unique $g:N\to H_A(M)$. For $a\in A$, $i_*(g\mu_a)=i_*(\mu_ag)$ and faithfulness make $g$ commute with every $\mu_a$; since sections of $A_Z$ are locally constant, $g$ is $A$-linear. Thus $g\mapsto\iota_M q_M^{-1}\,i_*g$, with $\iota_M:G(M)\hookrightarrow M$, is a bijection $\operatorname{Hom}(N,H_A(M))\cong\operatorname{Hom}(i_*N,M)$ of module maps. It is natural in $N$, and natural in $M$ by naturality of $q$ and of the kernel. So $i_*\dashv H_A$ on module sheaves, and at $g=\mathrm{id}$ its counit is $\iota_Mq_M^{-1}$, the support inclusion.

proof.text: For each etale object $V\to P$, the open immersion $V\times_PU\to V$ is a monomorphism in $P_{\mathrm{et}}$. The direct-image formula of [def-weil-pbc-direct-image] and the restriction/unit formula of [lem-weil-pbc-etale-inverse-image-restriction] identify $\eta_{j,I^r}(V)$ with $I^r(V)\to I^r(V\times_PU)$. These formulas hold on constant-$A$ modules: the actions and the adjunction unit have the same underlying formulas by [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact]. Apply [lem-pur-ringed-site-injective-mono-restriction] on the ringed site $(P_{\mathrm{et}},A_P)$ to the injective module sheaf $I^r$. This map is surjective. Thus $0\to G(I^r)\to I^r\to j_*j^*I^r\to0$ is exact in every degree. Naturality of the unit makes the differentials and every chain map preserve the kernels. Substitute Step 1's natural identification $G\cong i_*H_A$ and apply [lem-weil-pbc-cochain-complexes-degreewise-exact] to obtain the asserted short exact sequence of complexes and its naturality.

For $W=P,U,Z$, the category $\operatorname{Mod}(A_W)$ is Grothendieck abelian by [lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheaves-grothendieck]. Hence [lem-pur-kinjective-degreewise-existence] supplies functorial K-injective resolutions. An additive functor on sheaves acts on complexes and homotopies termwise, and preserves mapping cones and shifts. Indeed additivity identifies $F(Y^n\oplus X^{n+1})$ with $F(Y^n)\oplus F(X^{n+1})$ and carries the cone differential matrix to the corresponding matrix for $F(f)$; it also carries $-d$ to $-F(d)$. Thus it carries cone triangles to cone triangles, so its homotopy-category functor followed by derived localization is exact. Therefore [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-total-derived] applies to $H_A$ and to $j_*$ and computes their total unbounded right derived functors on K-injective complexes. In particular $H_A(I)$ computes $RH_A(L)$; no bounded-below replacement of $I$ has been made.

Because $i_*$ is exact and $i_*\dashv H_A$ by Step 1, [lem-weil-pbc-right-adjoint-preserves-kinjective] makes $H_A(I)$ K-injective. For a complex $N$ on $Z$ the natural bijections of [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived] and [lem-weil-pbc-termwise-adjunction-homotopy] give
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{D(P,A)}(i_*N,L)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{K(P,A)}(i_*N,I)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{K(Z,A)}(N,H_A(I))\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{D(Z,A)}(N,H_A(I)).$$
Exactness of $i_*$ allows its termwise application on the derived category, as in the statement. Thus $RH_A$ is its right adjoint, and the derived transpose of the identity of $H_A(I)$ is the localized support inclusion from Step 1. Compare this adjunction with the ordinary right adjoint $Ri_A^!$ of [lem-exc-closed-ambient]. By [det-sp-unique-right-adjoint] there is a unique natural counit-compatible isomorphism $RH_A\cong Ri_A^!$. This proves the first-term computation with its specified counit, not just an isomorphism of objects.

proof.text: The site equivalence $P_{\mathrm{et}}/U\simeq U_{\mathrm{et}}$ of [lem-weil-pbc-etale-site-localization-open] and the restriction formula of [lem-weil-pbc-etale-inverse-image-restriction] identify $j^*$ with localized restriction. The same equivalence applies to constant-$A$ modules: it transports the constant ring sheaf and its sectionwise actions. Hence [lem-pur-kinjective-restrict-localized] implies that $j^*I$ is K-injective, and Step 3 computes $Rj_*j^*L$ as $j_*j^*I$. Furthermore $j^*$ is exact and $j^*\dashv j_*$ by [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact], so [lem-weil-pbc-right-adjoint-preserves-kinjective] makes $j_*j^*I$ K-injective. For any K-injective $J$ on $U$, those same facts and the Hom bijections of [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived] and [lem-weil-pbc-termwise-adjunction-homotopy] give $\operatorname{Hom}_D(j^*N,QJ)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_K(j^*N,J)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_K(N,j_*J)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_D(QN,Qj_*J)$. This is the derived open adjunction. In particular, the unit at $L=QI$ is represented by $\eta_{j,I}:I\to j_*j^*I$: its transpose is the identity of $j^*I$. Thus the third-term comparison also identifies the second arrow with the actual derived unit.

Apply [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-triangle] to Step 2's short exact sequence. It gives a distinguished triangle with the support inclusion and open unit as its first two arrows. Its connecting morphism is the canonical short-exact-sequence boundary: if $a:i_*H_A(I)\to I$ is the inclusion and $q:\operatorname{Cone}(a)\to j_*j^*I$ the quotient map, then $\delta=(-p)q^{-1}$ in the cone convention of that cited lemma. For a chain map $I\to I'$, Step 2 gives the three maps of short exact sequences. Naturality in the cited lemma states exactly
$$ (i_*H_A(I\to I'))[1]\,\delta_I=\delta_{I'}\,(j_*j^*(I\to I')),$$
so these maps give a morphism of the entire triangles, including the connecting arrows. Steps 4 and 5 identify the endpoints and the first two arrows with $i_*Ri_A^!L$, $Rj_*j^*L$, the counit, and the unit. This supplies a realization of the counit/unit support triangle specified in the statement.

proof.text: These comparisons are independent of the representative in the derived sense. By [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived], a derived morphism between two K-injective representatives is represented by a unique homotopy class of chain maps; a quasi-isomorphism between such representatives is a homotopy equivalence. All termwise additive functors used above preserve homotopies (apply the functor to $f-g=dh+hd$). Consequently the three components of the triangle map in Step 6 depend only on the derived morphism, and a comparison between representatives gives an isomorphism of triangles. The first component remains counit-compatible by [det-sp-unique-right-adjoint], and the second and third remain the identity/comparison and the derived open-unit comparison from Step 5. This proves derived naturality as well as naturality for the chain maps in the statement. At no point did the argument require an underlying abelian sheaf, or a module sheaf after scalar restriction, to be injective.
